clue.text: To supply need, girl (saintly?) introduces gallon in load (12, three words)

parts.note: a girl's name, also that of St Bridget of Ireland, hence the saintly hint

indicators.note: one thing set in another is held inside it, so the gallon sits within the load

parts.note: a heap is a load or pile
G is the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: A saintly girl brings a gallon into a load, as if to meet some charitable need.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl introduces the rest by coming first; the gallon then goes inside the load.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge the gap is an idiom for filling a shortfall, which is supplying what is needed.

clue.text: Bread roll — stock ordered in — Irish one's had much exposure

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the Irish backstop of the Brexit talks

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the stock is reshuffled
these letters are placed inside the bread roll

parts.note: a bap is a soft British bread roll
the letters of stock rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopping-list jumble of bread rolls and stock, with an Irish one oddly overexposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish backstop was the fallback arrangement for the Irish border in the 2019 Brexit negotiations, endlessly discussed in the news; the reshuffled stock goes in after BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstop was the name for the Northern Ireland border guarantee that dominated Brexit headlines, so it had huge media exposure.

clue.text: Regret endless journey over waterway, caring for some country clergy

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a ride is a journey
a canal is an artificial waterway

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a never-ending trip along a canal while looking after rural parsons.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part above the waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruridecanal means relating to a rural dean, who has charge of the clergy of a group of country parishes.

clue.text: Doing without professional help bags IOM trophy — some catch!

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it into a bag, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: do-it-yourself
the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An amateur scoops the Isle of Man trophy, and what a catch that would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a prize or a cricket catch, but a catch is also a round sung by several voices.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a type of song, a round, and a ditty is a short simple song, so the exclamation flags a loose example.

clue.text: Bent structure, last removed from class

indicators.note: taking away the last means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification

explanation.surface: A curved structure has had its final element taken out of a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Genu is the anatomical Latin for the knee, the jointed structure that bends.

clue.text: Lunge awkwardly in river for primitive creature there?

indicators.note: these letters go inside the river word
doing something awkwardly makes it come out clumsy and disordered, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of lunge rearranged
ea is a dialect word for a river, given in Chambers

explanation.surface: Something lunges clumsily in a river, perhaps a primitive creature living there.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'there' tie the definition to the river: this tiny organism lives in fresh water.
explanation.definitionFit: Euglena is a single-celled freshwater organism with a whip-like flagellum, a primitive form of life.

clue.text: Voluntary fee, ancient and not limited

definitions.note: an obsolete noun sense, equal to honorarium

indicators.note: something limited is hemmed in on both sides, so the conjunction is held within the other word

parts.note: hoary means very old
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A voluntary payment is described as ancient and unrestricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not limited' reads as one phrase, but 'and not' gives one word and 'limited' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists an old noun use of the word for an honorarium, a fee paid voluntarily rather than by obligation.

clue.text: Sudden rise in water rate agreed in part

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A sudden jump in the water rate has been partly agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water rate' looks like a bill, but water belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave that surges suddenly up a river such as the Trent.

clue.text: Flying locust sucked into Greek plane's safety mechanism

indicators.note: drawn inside, so these letters sit within the abbreviation
something flying about is scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of locust rearranged
GK is the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: A locust gets sucked into the engine of a Greek airliner, a safety worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' looks Greek-owned, but the Greek is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust lock clamps an aircraft's control surfaces while parked so wind cannot damage them.

clue.text: Countryman's jumped up having caught a young trout

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
to catch something is to hold it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: lep is a dialect past tense of leap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rustic leapt up after landing a small trout.
explanation.walkthrough: The countryman marks the dialect form; the A goes inside it before the whole is turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a peal is a grilse or young sea trout.

clue.text: Foreign girlfriend and wife, about united, on the best of terms (7, two words)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the letter for united

parts.note: amie is French for a female friend
U is the abbreviation for united
ux. is the abbreviation for uxor, Latin for wife

explanation.surface: A man's French girlfriend and his wife, it seems, are united and on excellent terms.
explanation.walkthrough: UX, short for uxor, is the legal abbreviation for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Au mieux is a French phrase adopted in English meaning on the most intimate or friendly footing.

clue.text: Sort of hovercraft, power in test failing — it may cover treads (11, two words)

indicators.note: something failing falls apart, so these letters break up and rearrange
these pieces go inside the rearranged word

parts.note: the letters of test rearranged
an air-car is a vehicle riding on a cushion of air
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A hovercraft prototype fails its power test.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the air-car and the power letter sit inside the reshuffled test.
explanation.definitionFit: Treads are the flat steps of a staircase, and a stair carpet is laid over them.

clue.text: Old vulgarian holding end of cigar — it's often lit

indicators.note: holding something means it is kept inside

parts.note: cit is an old contemptuous word for a townsman, a vulgar tradesman

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of cigar

explanation.surface: A boorish old fellow holds the end of his cigar, which is often lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit' seems to belong with the cigar, but it is short for literary: crit often follows it in lit crit.
explanation.definitionFit: Crit is short for criticism, and literary criticism is commonly shortened to lit crit.

clue.text: Rap singer, good one but full of unease about our lot

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
angst is anxiety about the human condition
a means one

explanation.surface: A rapper who is a decent sort but troubled by existential worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or reversal signal but belongs inside the phrase meaning existential dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsta is the style of rap about gang life, and the word is also applied to a performer of it.

clue.text: Outfit and curved sabre abandoned by war in palm tree

parts.note: kit is an outfit of clothes or gear

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a tulwar is an Indian curved sabre
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kit and a sabre lie discarded after the fighting in a palm grove.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittul is the jaggery palm of India and Sri Lanka, source of a fibre and sugar.

clue.text: One entering left twice (in different guises) — a grand entrance

indicators.note: something entering goes into another, so it ends up inside

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a means one
L is the usual abbreviation for left, a second guise of the same word

explanation.surface: A newcomer passes the same spot twice in disguise before making a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is used twice, once as the nautical word and once as its abbreviation, and the one goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a large, imposing doorway or gate.

clue.text: Large vessel filling basin drunk, recalling wild night in Dundee?

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and muddled, so these letters are jumbled
a filling sits inside something, so the vessel goes within

parts.note: the letters of basin rearranged
an urn is a large vessel

explanation.surface: A boozy night in Dundee ends with a large pot filling a basin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a hint by example: Burns's Tam o' Shanter tells of a drunken wild night, and Dundee places it in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnsian means in the manner of the poet Robert Burns, whose verse recalls riotous Scottish nights.

clue.text: Page-turner giving one tense time (short), not so good

indicators.note: short means shortened, so the word loses letters to its abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar
an hour is a time
iller is a comparative of ill, meaning worse

explanation.surface: A gripping novel gives its reader a tense, if brief, time that ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' and 'time' read as a description of the novel, but each is a separate building piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so exciting you keep reading, and a thriller is the classic example.

clue.text: English and Latin included in rigidly formal exam

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
E is the abbreviation for English
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: English and Latin papers set in a stiff, formal examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelim is a preliminary examination, such as a first-year university exam.

clue.text: A motet's so stirring, though lacking tenor, in grand style

indicators.note: stirring moves things around, so the remaining letters are mixed
lacking something means going without it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A motet moves the listener even without its tenor line, sounding majestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as moving praise for the music, but it tells you to mix the letters once a T is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is a musical direction meaning majestic, to be played in a stately manner.

clue.text: Scot's resolute for all to see, getting into college

indicators.note: getting into a place means going inside it

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A determined Scot makes his way into college in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for a film suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Teuch is a Scots form of tough, meaning hardy or resolute.

clue.text: A keg fashioned with this whitewood? Ageing oak possibly

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped from material, so the keg and the answer together are made from reworked letters
possibly signals one arrangement among several, so the letters of the oak phrase can be reordered
the answer plus the keg make up the jumbled letters, so the keg is taken away to leave it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cooper builds a keg from this pale timber, perhaps aged oak.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: A KEG together with the answer rearranges into AGEING OAK, so remove those four letters from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a New Zealand tree with light white timber, so whitewood describes it.

clue.text: Derbyshire location, one Bertie found forbidding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a market town in the Peak District
second meaning: Sir Roderick, the nerve specialist in the Wodehouse stories who terrifies Bertie Wooster

explanation.surface: A Derbyshire spot that someone named Bertie found off-putting.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie is Bertie Wooster of P. G. Wodehouse's comic novels, who calls the formidable Sir Roderick an alarming old bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Derbyshire town and to the intimidating brain specialist in Wodehouse's Jeeves stories.

clue.text: Runs test showing early signs of damp

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Running checks reveal the first traces of damp in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early signs of damp' suggests a surveyor's report, but it means the dew of early morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Roral is a rare word meaning dewy, and dew is the morning's first moisture.

clue.text: Scout rule? Look after that

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rule
ecce is Latin for behold

explanation.surface: A Scout leader recites a rule and then says to look at what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After that' puts the Latin word behind the rule abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is a reconnaissance, a scouting trip, and to scout is to carry one out.

clue.text: What'll spell depression for Indian scholar?

parts.note: surface reading: something that will bring on a spell of low mood
setter's reading: split the answer into a letter, a conjunction and a pronoun, and the letter and pronoun spell a word for a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Something that brings on a spell of gloom for an Indian scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as P AND IT: P and IT together spell PIT, a depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandit is a learned Hindu, a scholar or teacher, the source of English pundit.

clue.text: Last of meal stored in handy earthenware

indicators.note: something stored in a place is kept inside it

parts.note: deft means skilful with the hands

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of meal

explanation.surface: The remains of a meal are put away in a convenient earthenware dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is tin-glazed earthenware, typically blue and white, originally from the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: Copy as alternative to period (reverse thereof)

indicators.note: reverse tells you to turn the preceding phrase back to front

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
per. is an abbreviation for period

explanation.surface: A copy is offered as an alternative to a period piece, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse thereof' sounds like a note about the comparison, but it turns the phrase back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original, especially of furniture or a print.

clue.text: Saint, one seen hiding in a tree

indicators.note: someone hiding in a place is concealed inside it

parts.note: the article a, written an before a vowel
one saint, S being the abbreviation for saint
the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A saint is spotted hiding up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the saint, so it gives S; 'a tree' must be read as AN ELM for the letters to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm was an eleventh-century Archbishop of Canterbury and theologian.

clue.text: General's assistant bags century batting for both sides

indicators.note: to bag something is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an ADC is an aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A general's aide makes a hundred while batting for both teams in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a century hides a slang sense: batting for both sides means bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, from alternating and direct current, and batting for both sides is an idiom for the same.

clue.text: Sluggish Scottish river dam retained by stone

indicators.note: what is retained is held in, so these letters are kept inside

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
a weir is a low dam across a river

explanation.surface: A slow Scottish river is held back by a stone-built dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish river' looks like a unit, but the Scottish belongs to the definition and the river to the dam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweirt is a Scots word meaning lazy or reluctant, so it labels someone slow and idle.

clue.text: Distortion? This roof is able to withstand onset

indicators.note: the answer followed by the roof word makes the phrase, so remove that word to leave the answer

parts.note: proof against attack, onset meaning an assault
taken as written

explanation.surface: A roof that holds up against the first onslaught of weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus ROOF makes WAR-PROOF, able to resist attack; the blog notes Chambers actually defines war-proof differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A warp is a twist or bend out of shape, which is a distortion.

clue.text: Fowl à la française cooked in allspice (not soft inside)

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed
taking away an inner soft letter means one middle letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Birds prepared French-style, cooked in allspice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cailles is French for quails, small game birds, so they are fowl as a French cook would name them.

clue.text: Large fruit, juice nil

parts.note: juice in the sense of energy, vigour
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A big fruit that yields no juice at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juice' means liquid in the surface, but here it is slang for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepo is the fleshy many-seeded fruit of the gourd family, such as a melon or pumpkin.

clue.text: I err badly because going round hollows in Cairngorms?

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in the wrong order
going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: cos is short for because
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A hillwalker admits going wrong by wandering round the Cairngorms.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the Cairngorms as an example: a corrie is a Scottish mountain hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Corries are steep-sided, bowl-shaped glacial hollows on Scottish mountains like the Cairngorms.

clue.text: Live model's pose? No charge when (not initially very) melodious family's involved!

indicators.note: something involved is drawn into the middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: a charge is a cost

indicators.note: without its initial means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
the singing family of The Sound of Music
O for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A life model poses for free while the musical von Trapps are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: COST O means a charge of nothing; the von Trapps lose their V and go inside after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrapposto is the classical sculptural pose with weight on one leg and the torso twisted, as a life model might hold.
